# Make the test suite pass

`catalog/` is a small library-catalog package with a test suite under `tests/`.
The suite is currently failing in several places.

Run it:

```
python3 -m unittest
```

Work through the failures and fix the code in `catalog/` until the whole suite
passes. The tests describe the intended behavior — treat them as the
specification and do not modify them.

Done when `python3 -m unittest` reports every test passing.
output_tail:
[tool: bash]
[tool: bash]
Emma's author/year: Jane Austen, 1815 (consistent with test_search data).
[tool: bash]
All 16 tests now pass when I run `python3 -m unittest`. I didn't change any test files. Before the fixes, 15 tests ran and 10 of them failed. The 16th test only appeared after the search fix below, because that test module couldn't be imported at all before.

| File | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `catalog/search.py` | It imported from `catalog.nonexistent`, which doesn't exist, so the whole search test module failed to load | Now imports `normalize` from `catalog.text` |
| `catalog/books.py` | `parse_book` kept the year as text (`'1965'`), so `age()` crashed | The year is now converted to a number |
| `catalog/factory.py` | The sample data had 2 books but the docstring says 3 | Added `Book("Emma", "Austen", 1815, 1)` |
| `catalog/fees.py` | It added days and the daily fee instead of multiplying them (1 day late cost 1.25 instead of 0.25) | Now `days_late * DAILY_FEE` |
| `catalog/inventory.py` | `recent(n)` returned one event too many (`[-n - 1:]`) | Now `[-n:]`, and returns an empty list when `n <= 0` |
| `catalog/members.py` | `MAX_BORROWED` was 3, but the comment and tests say 5 | Set to 5 |

Two things in these fixes go beyond what the tests specify:
- The tests only check Emma's title. I took the author and year (Austen, 1815) from the search tests and gave it 1 copy, which was my own choice.
- I added the `n <= 0` case in `recent` myself. Without it, `[-0:]` would have returned the whole history.

The folder isn't a git repository, so the edits are only on disk.
